summary: Pulsar 2849 is a dice-drafting space euro where players draft dice from a shared communal pool to fuel technology, exploration, and infrastructure tracks. It offers multiple parallel paths to victory and rewards efficient engine-building over an eight-round arc.
praised: Clever dice-drafting mechanism where die value and color both matter
Multiple distinct paths to victory keep games varied
Satisfying engine-building feel with tech tree upgrades
Elegant, tight ruleset for the depth it offers
criticised: Can feel dry and heavily systems-focused with little theme
Some strategies (e.g., certain tech combos) seen as stronger in analysis
Dice availability can feel swingy if the pool doesn't favor your plan
Player interaction is fairly indirect for some tastes

interaction.kind: drafting from a shared pool of dice and racing to claim unique pulsar/planet tiles
interaction.detail: Each round's dice are a communal pool, so taking the die you want can leave an opponent with a worse choice, and pulsars/technologies are limited unique tiles that go to whoever claims them first. Beyond that contested draft and claim, most turns are spent building your own private tableau of technologies and orbits.
interaction.said: unknown — generally described as a smooth, satisfying engine-builder rather than a game people call mean

subsystems: gyrodyne/pulsar power production (repeating per-round VP from spinning gyrodynes and completed transmitters)
colony network development (nonlinear area-growth bonus for stations built across planetary systems)
technology and goal-tile objectives (purchased tech cards and chosen goal tiles paying out end-game VP)
sources: spinning gyrodyne value scored every round (1/2/3 VP each)
uncompleted (non-spinning) gyrodynes and unclaimed pulsars (1VP each at game end)
colonies/stations on the board (nonlinear scale, e.g. 2→2VP, 8→20VP, 13→50VP, +3VP each beyond)
initiative track final standing (7/4/2 VP for 1st/2nd/3rd)
scoring.how_you_win: Over a fixed 8 rounds you rack up VP each round from your spinning gyrodynes and transmitters, then add end-game VP for colonies built, technologies bought, goal tiles completed, pulsars claimed, initiative-track placement, and leftover cubes; highest total wins.
